final.question: The site reads like your own documentation habits — a job card for projects, a logbook for skills, an exploded view for how things are built — rather than a portfolio-agency performance of them.
final.form: The co-op job card (Reported / Found / Parts or build / Work done / Result, with Result allowed to read 'pending') and the workshop logbook, reused as the layout of the project sections and the skills list.

swap.reason: The scaffold is taken from her own two documents — the co-op job card and the workshop logbook — and the 3D is her specific pedal box bracket, so it would not transplant unchanged to another second-year engineer.

backdrop.reason: The exploded bracket carries per-part callouts and its end state (laid out flat, never reassembled) is what encodes the part's unmachined status, so deleting it loses evidence, not just scenery — though the hero's idle rotation is admitted decoration.

depth.reason: After the hero the page is a project list — bracket, charger, co-op, Slow Miles, skills, contact could be reordered with nothing lost; the only beginning-middle-end arc lives inside section 2.

clipart.reason: The 3D subjects are her own pedal box mounting bracket and the charger's gear train, not a stock emblem of engineering such as a gear-wheel motif or hard hat.

honesty.reason: The final plan dates the 12th place as July 2025 'before I joined', marks the 18% as CAD and simulation with machining pending, credits the charger to a group of four, drops the bike count to tenure, and adds nothing invented.

thirty_seconds.reason: The hero holds name, course, institution, the placement line, CV download and email with no scroll and no animation gating, and the CV/email affordance persists down the page.

plain_reader.reason: The opening is her name, course, year and 'Looking for a summer 2026 placement in mechanical or product design' — plain enough for any reader and not overclaiming to an engineer.

judgement.summary: This is a restrained, two-minute-reader plan that borrows Mina's own job card and logbook as the layout of her project sections, pairs them with an exploded-view 3D render of the pedal box bracket, and ends up scrupulously honest once her corrections land — dated team result, CAD-only 18%, group credit on the charger, no bike count, nothing invented. Its greatest weakness is that honesty and form were retrofitted rather than designed in: the first reply printed "hundreds of bikes fixed", treated 12th of 68 and the untested 18% as her own hard metrics, and the final page is still an orderless project list whose 3D splits into two unrelated scenes instead of one object carried through the scroll.
